studies.title: [Insights on biological markers in post-COVID condition: a scope review].
studies.authors: Amorim, Amanda Dos Santos de, Porto, Evailson Ferreira, Oliveira, Márcio Vasconcelos
studies.abstract: Post-COVID condition (PCC) is characterized by the persistence of symptoms following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. This scoping review aimed to identify and compile scientific evidence on biomarkers associated with PCC to elucidate its pathophysiology and support clinical diagnosis and management. A systematic search was conducted in six databases (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase, and ScienceDirect), selecting original studies published between May 2020 and April 2024. Observational studies investigating clinical and prognostic biomarkers in PCC patients were included. After applying eligibility criteria, 10 studies were selected. The most frequently reported biomarkers were interleukins IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8, proteins associated with persistent inflammation and immune dysfunction. Other relevant markers included D-dimer, C-reactive protein (CRP), VEGF-A, and matrix metalloproteinases. Results highlight that inflammatory biomarkers play a key role in characterizing and monitoring PCC. It is concluded that identifying accessible biomarkers, easily integrated into clinical practice, can aid in developing more effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. A condição pós-COVID (CPC) é caracterizada pela persistência de sintomas após a infecção aguda pelo SARS-CoV-2. Esta revisão de escopo teve como objetivo identificar e reunir evidências científicas sobre biomarcadores associados à CPC, visando esclarecer sua fisiopatologia e apoiar o diagnóstico e manejo clínico. A busca sistemática foi realizada em seis bases de dados (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase e ScienceDirect), selecionando artigos originais publicados entre maio de 2020 e abril de 2024. Foram incluídos estudos observacionais que investigaram biomarcadores clínicos e prognósticos em pacientes com CPC. Após a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade, 10 estudos foram selecionados. Os biomarcadores mais frequentemente relatados foram as interleucinas IL-1β, IL-6 e IL-8, interleucinas associadas à inflamação persistente e disfunção imunológica. Outros marcadores relevantes incluíram D-dímero, proteína C reativa (PCR), VEGF-A e metaloproteinases. Os resultados reforçam que os biomarcadores inflamatórios desempenham papel essencial na caracterização e monitoramento da CPC. Conclui-se que a identificação de biomarcadores acessíveis e integráveis à prática clínica pode auxiliar na elaboração de estratégias diagnósticas e terapêuticas mais eficazes. La condición post-COVID (CPC) se caracteriza por la persistencia de síntomas tras la infección aguda por SARS-CoV-2. Esta revisión de alcance tuvo como objetivo identificar y recopilar evidencia científica sobre biomarcadores asociados con la CPC, con el fin de esclarecer su fisiopatología y apoyar el diagnóstico y manejo clínico. Se realizó una búsqueda sistemática en seis bases de datos (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase y ScienceDirect), seleccionando estudios originales publicados entre mayo de 2020 y abril de 2024. Se incluyeron estudios observacionales que investigaron biomarcadores clínicos y pronósticos en pacientes con CPC. Tras aplicar los criterios de elegibilidad, se seleccionaron 10 estudios. Los biomarcadores más frecuentemente reportados fueron las interleucinas IL-1β, IL-6 e IL-8, proteínas asociadas con inflamación persistente y disfunción inmunológica. Otros marcadores relevantes incluyeron D-dímero, proteína C reactiva (PCR), VEGF-A y metaloproteinasas. Los resultados destacan que los biomarcadores inflamatorios desempeñan un papel clave en la caracterización y el monitoreo de la CPC. Se concluye que la identificación de biomarcadores accesibles e integrables en la práctica clínica puede contribuir al desarrollo de estrategias diagnósticas y terapéuticas más eficaces.

studies.title: Risk factors for Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in patients hospitalized for severe acute respiratory syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.authors: Soares, Sofia Ramos, Souza, Rafaela Santos Nogueira de, Barros, Loreena Uchôa Lira, Camboim, Felipe Miranda et al.
studies.abstract: This study aims to identify the risk factors associated with the development of post-COVID-19 syndrome in patients discharged from hospitalizations due to severe acute respiratory syndrome. A systematic review of observational studies published between 2020 and 2023 was carried out in six databases. The relative risk values of each factor investigated were evaluated in the meta-analysis using the random-effects model; 1,010 publications were identified, with 45 studies included in the qualitative analysis and seven studies in the meta-analysis. These studies evaluated the association between post-COVID-19 syndrome and factors such as the severity and number of symptoms of the disease in the acute phase, sex, and previous comorbidities. The results showed that female gender (RR 1.52; 95%CI 1.26-1.85), the presence of hypertension (RR 1.25; 95%CI 1.06-1.49) and a longer hospital stay (RR 1.01; 95%CI 1.01-1.03) were associated with the development of the syndrome. Female patients discharged from hospital due to COVID-19, with longer hospital stays and hypertension should be monitored to identify the development of post-COVID-19 syndrome, enabling timely interventions. Este estudo tem como objetivo identificar os fatores de risco associados ao desenvolvimento da síndrome pós-COVID-19 em egressos de internações por Síndrome Respiratória Aguda Grave. Foi realizada revisão sistemática de estudos observacionais publicados entre 2020 e 2023 em seis bases de dados. Os valores dos riscos relativos de cada fator investigado foram avaliados na metanálise através do modelo de efeitos aleatórios; 1.010 publicações foram identificadas, sendo 45 estudos incluídos na análise qualitativa e sete estudos na metanálise. Estes estudos avaliaram a associação entre a síndrome pós-COVID-19 e fatores como a gravidade e o número de sintomas da doença na fase aguda, o sexo e comorbidades prévias. Os resultados apontaram que o sexo feminino (RR 1,52; IC95% 1,26-1,85), a presença de hipertensão (RR 1,25; IC95% 1,06-1,49) e um maior tempo de internação (RR 1,01; IC95% 1.01-1,03) estavam associados ao desenvolvimento da síndrome. Egressos de internação por COVID-19 do sexo feminino, com maior tempo de internação e hipertensão deverão ser monitorados para identificar o desenvolvimento da síndrome pós-COVID-19, possibilitando intervenções em tempo oportuno. Este estudio tiene como objetivo identificar los factores de riesgo asociados al desarrollo del síndrome post-COVID-19 en pacientes dados de alta de hospitalizaciones por síndrome respiratorio agudo severo. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de estudios observacionales publicados entre 2020 y 2023 en seis bases de datos. Los valores de riesgo relativo de cada factor investigado se evaluaron en el metaanálisis utilizando un modelo de efectos aleatorios. Se identificaron 1.010 publicaciones, de las cuales 45 estudios se incluyeron en el análisis cualitativo y siete en el metaanálisis. Estos estudios evaluaron la asociación entre el síndrome post-COVID-19 y factores como la gravedad y el número de síntomas de la enfermedad en la fase aguda, el sexo y las comorbilidades preexistentes. Los resultados indicaron que el sexo femenino (RR 1,52; IC95% 1,26-1,85), la presencia de hipertensión (RR 1,25; IC95% 1,06-1,49) y una estancia hospitalaria más prolongada (RR 1,01; IC95% 1,01-1,03) se asociaron con el desarrollo del síndrome. Las pacientes dadas de alta tras una hospitalización por COVID-19, con estancias hospitalarias más prolongadas e hipertensión, deben ser monitorizadas para identificar el desarrollo del síndrome post-COVID-19 y permitir intervenciones oportunas.

studies.title: [Death from post-COVID-19 conditions in Brazil: a descriptive study, 2020-2023].
studies.authors: Couto, Rodrigo de Macedo, Boing, Alexandra Crispim
studies.abstract: Little is known about the magnitude of deaths and which comorbidities may contribute to the occurrence of outcomes among individuals with post-COVID conditions. This study aimed to identify deaths due to post-COVID conditions in Brazil from 2020 to 2023 and describe the consequential and contributing causes. A descriptive study was conducted using ICD-10 codes B94.8 and U09.9. Between 2020 and 2023, Brazil reported 6,911,833 deaths. Of these, 5,017 (0.07%) were related to post-COVID conditions. The peak occurred in the 2nd quarter of 2021, with an average decline of 28% in the subsequent quarters. The highest mortality rate was in the Central-West region, except in 2020, when the highest rate was in the North region. Tocantins had the highest annual mortality rates, except in 2021, when Espírito Santo recorded the highest number. Most deaths occurred among white individuals, the elderly, and those with higher education levels. The most common consequential causes were septicemia (42.9%) and respiratory events (52.8%). Among the contributing causes, diabetes mellitus was notable (20.5%). The study reveals a significant number of deaths due to post-COVID-19 conditions in Brazil, highlighting regional variations and marked sociodemographic differences. Pouco se sabe sobre a magnitude dos óbitos e quais comorbidades podem contribuir para a ocorrência do desfecho entre pessoas com condições pós-COVID. Este estudo teve como objetivo identificar os óbitos por condições pós-COVID no Brasil no período de 2020 a 2023 e descrever as causas consequenciais e contribuintes. Delineou-se um estudo descritivo utilizando os códigos CID-10 B94.8 e U09.9. Entre 2020 e 2023, foram notificados 6.911.833 óbitos no Brasil. Desses, 5.017 (0,07%) estavam relacionados a condições pós-COVID. O pico ocorreu no 2° trimestre de 2021, com uma queda média de 28% nos trimestres subsequentes. A maior taxa de mortalidade foi na região Centro-Oeste, exceto em 2020, quando a maior taxa foi na região Norte. O estado de Tocantins teve as maiores taxas anuais de mortalidade, exceto em 2021, quando o estado de Espírito Santo registrou o maior número. A maioria dos óbitos ocorreu entre pessoas brancas, idosos e pessoas com maior escolaridade. As causas consequenciais mais comuns foram septicemia (42,9%) e eventos respiratórios (52,8%). Entre as causas contribuintes, destacou-se o diabetes mellitus (20,5%). O estudo revela um número importante de óbitos por condições pós-COVID-19 no Brasil, evidenciando variações regionais e diferenças sociodemográficas marcantes. Poco se sabe acerca de la magnitud de las muertes y comorbilidades que pueden contribuir a la ocurrencia del desenlace en personas con condiciones posteriores a la COVID-19. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo identificar los fallecimientos atribuibles a condiciones post-COVID en Brasil entre los años 2020 y 2023, y describir sus causas consecuentes y contribuyentes. Se diseñó un estudio descriptivo utilizando los códigos CIE-10 B94.8 y U09.9. Entre 2020 y 2023, donde fueron notificadas 6.911.833 muertes en Brasil, de las cuales 5.017 (0,07%) estuvieron relacionadas con condiciones post-COVID. El pico de muertes se registró en el segundo trimestre de 2021, seguido por una disminución media del 28 % en los trimestres posteriores. La mayor tasa de mortalidad se observó en la región Centro-Oeste, con excepción para 2020, cuando la región Norte presentó la mayor tasa. El estado de Tocantins registró las tasas anuales más elevadas de mortalidad, salvo en 2021, año en que el estado de Espírito Santo reportó el mayor número de fallecimientos. La mayoría de las muertes ocurrieron entre personas blancas, personas mayores y personas con mayor nivel educativo. Las causas consecuentes más frecuentes fueron la septicemia (42,9 %) y los eventos respiratorios (52,8 %). Entre las causas contribuyentes, se destacó la diabetes mellitus (20,5 %). El estudio revela un número significativo de muertes por condiciones post-COVID-19 en Brasil, poniendo de manifiesto importantes variaciones regionales y marcadas diferencias sociodemográficas.

studies.title: Tuberculous meningoencephalitis in a heart transplant recipient: a case report.
studies.authors: Ferreira, Lucas Teixeira Fazio, Favato, Gileyre Rinaldi, Bittante, Carolina Devite, Bacal, Fernando et al.
studies.abstract: A 33-year-old woman who had undergone heart transplantation two years earlier for post-COVID-19 myocarditis was admitted with decompensated heart failure secondary to acute antibody-mediated rejection. During hospitalization, she developed sepsis, cytomegalovirus infection, acute kidney injury, and an incidental pulmonary miliary pattern on chest computed tomography, without microbiological confirmation. After stabilization, approximately six months later, she presented with headache, fever, and focal neurological signs. Meningoencephalitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis was diagnosed based on a positive molecular test of the cerebrospinal fluid, and antituberculous therapy was started, resulting in clinical improvement and discharge. Four months later, she was readmitted with decreased consciousness, and relapse associated with cerebral vasculitis was identified and attributed to poor treatment adherence. Therapy was restarted and continued for 12 months, with a favorable outcome. This case highlights the diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive challenges of central nervous system tuberculosis in heavily immunosuppressed solid organ transplant recipients.

studies.title: More common than we thought: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, comorbidity burden, and long COVID risk in a national cohort.
studies.authors: Pearson, Megan L, Laraway, Bryan J, Elias, Ellen R, Bilousova, Ganna et al.
studies.abstract: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) is a complex, underdiagnosed connective tissue disorder characterized by widespread symptoms affecting multiple organ systems. Recent clinical observations suggest that individuals with hEDS may be at increased risk for persistent symptoms following COVID-19, commonly referred to as Long COVID. Using data from over 19 million patients across the United States, we examined associations between hEDS, COVID-19 infection, Long COVID, and related chronic conditions. We identified just over 25,000 individuals with hEDS and estimated a prevalence of approximately 1 in 800, which is higher than previously recognized. Despite similar rates of COVID-19 infection between patients with hEDS and matched controls, patients with hEDS were nearly three times more likely to develop Long COVID. This risk was concentrated among patients with hEDS who also had overlapping conditions commonly seen in post-viral syndromes, including autonomic dysfunction (POTS), immune dysregulation (MCAS), and chronic fatigue (ME/CFS). Patients with hEDS also exhibited higher odds of having additional risk factors for severe or prolonged illness, including chronic lung and autoimmune conditions, depression, and cerebrovascular disease. A subgroup of patients received their hEDS diagnosis only after a COVID-19 or Long COVID diagnosis, and this subgroup was highly enriched for multimorbidity, particularly POTS and MCAS. These findings establish hEDS as more prevalent than previously recognized and identify a substantially elevated, comorbidity-driven risk of Long COVID in this population. Improved screening, earlier diagnosis, and integrated care pathways are urgently needed to support this complex and underserved patient group.

studies.title: Single-cell and spatial characterization of the human pancreas in cystic fibrosis.
studies.authors: Mummey, Hannah M, Corban, Sierra, Lucero, Jacinta, Melton, Rebecca L et al.
studies.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) causes severely damaged pancreatic morphology and cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD), but the cellular drivers of CFRD in the pancreas are not understood. Here, we perform single-cell and spatial profiling of 2.04 M cells from 23 non-disease or CF pancreas donors. A high-mucin ductal sub-type had relatively preserved abundance and genomic profiles but altered localization in CF. Changes in inflammatory and fibrotic pathways were driven by crosstalk between immune and pro-fibrotic cells in specific niches. Beta cells had extensive changes in CF, including increased stress responses and evidence for compensatory secretion, that were distinct from those in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Islets localized near large adipose tissue and collagen in CF had reduced beta cells linked to signaling from adipocytes, macrophages, stellate cells, and high-mucin ductal cells. Overall, our results highlight pancreatic microenvironments of beta cell dysfunction in CF and offer in-roads to preserving beta cells in CFRD.

studies.title: Rehabilitation professionals at the COVID-19 frontline: a testimony-informed narrative review of health-worker mortality, vaccine hesitancy, physiotherapy and telerehabilitation.
studies.authors: Npochinto Moumeni, Ibrahim
studies.abstract: COVID-19 placed an unprecedented burden on health workers and disrupted rehabilitation services. Existing reviews have examined health-worker infection and mortality, vaccine hesitancy and telerehabilitation separately; few have considered these dimensions together from the perspective of rehabilitation professionals. Narrative review following SANRA recommendations. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched (initial search January 2019-December 2022; updated during revision to December 2025 to capture later publications reporting 2020-2021 data). Sources were selected purposively, prioritising systematic reviews, large multicentre studies and official agency reports. First-person clinical observations from the author's postgraduate training in two French university hospitals are presented separately, in labelled boxes, and are not used as evidence for quantitative claims. WHO estimated 80,000-180,000 health and care worker deaths from COVID-19 between January 2020 and May 2021 (central estimate 115,500), versus 6,643 reported through surveillance. Front-line workers had a 3.4-fold higher adjusted risk of a positive test than the general community. Vaccine hesitancy among health workers was 37% in a 91-country survey and 22.5% in a review of 76,471 workers; a scoping review of nurses reported 20.7% refusal. In a French tertiary centre, 73.1% were in favour, 23.1% hesitant and 3.9% opposed. Physiotherapy guidance addressed acute respiratory care, early mobilisation and post-COVID-19 rehabilitation. Telerehabilitation achieved outcomes similar to centre-based pulmonary rehabilitation, but accounted for only 6% of outpatient episodes in a large US database. Four heuristic constructs are proposed: Frontline Abandonment Syndrome (FAS), Vaccination Refusal Cascade (VRC), Telerehabilitation Emergency Pivot (TEP) and Post-COVID Functional Decoupling (PCFD). Each is positioned against existing terminology and presented as a testable hypothesis rather than a validated construct. COVID-19 exposed gaps in health-worker protection, communication around vaccination and the integration of rehabilitation into pandemic preparedness. Telerehabilitation deserves a defined place in hybrid care models, and the proposed constructs require formal concept analysis and empirical testing.

studies.title: Management of Rhino-Orbital-Cerebral Mucormycosis Infection: Anesthetic Challenges.
studies.authors: Imantalab, Vali, Dodangeh Balakhani, Mohammad, Haghani, Iman, Rahmanian, Nazanin et al.
studies.abstract: Despite the application of surgery and antifungal therapy, rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis is a severe and life-threatening fungal infection with high morbidity and mortality rates, particularly in immunocompromised patients. This review aimed to focus on the current evidence on perioperative anesthetic management of rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM), emphasizing the unique challenges posed by its aggressive, angioinvasive nature. Key issues included difficult airway management due to fungal debris and supraglottic edema, hemodynamic instability, renal dysfunction from nephrotoxic antifungal therapy (e.g., amphotericin B), and the critical need for glycemic control in diabetic patients. Case studies have illustrated the complexities of managing comorbidities, such as post-COVID-19 sequelae, uncontrolled diabetes, and immunosuppression. Preoperative optimization, judicious management of fluids and electrolytes, and the use of video laryngoscopy for difficult intubation are highly recommended. By addressing these challenges, this article provided a practical framework for anesthesiologists to enhance perioperative care in patients with ROCM, ultimately improving survival and reducing complications. Awareness of these procedures may help clinicians choose the most effective treatment regimens. However, further studies are warranted to correlate these findings with clinical outcomes.

studies.title: Effectiveness of an Extension for Community Health Outcomes case-based virtual community of practice model on clinician outcomes for the management of long COVID and fatiguing illnesses: a randomized control trial.
studies.authors: Zuber, Alexandra, Rothwell, Jonathan T, Samaniego, Jane C, Sharp, Sydney P et al.
studies.abstract: Patients with Long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions (IACC) often face barriers to accessing specialist care, prompting the need to strengthen primary care capacity to manage these complex conditions. Our study evaluated the effectiveness of an ECHO case-based virtual community of practice model for improving clinician knowledge, confidence, and practice for Long COVID and other IACC in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) [Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05167227)]. The study was a two-arm, single-blind, cluster RCT; intervention clinicians were invited to participate in weekly case-based, interactive, expert-led virtual learning sessions focused on patient care for individuals with Long COVID and other IACC. Intervention and control groups were also invited to monthly interactive webinars and quarterly short courses. Virtual learning occurred on Zoom videoconferencing software. Data were collected from routine clinician surveys, participation records, and electronic health records. The analysis identified treatment effects using generalized linear models predicting scaled scores for knowledge, changes to practice, and confidence in the management of patients with Long COVID and other IACC. Adjusting for baseline controls, the intervention group achieved significantly higher levels of knowledge (standardized beta coefficient: b = 0.77, 95% CI 0.20 to 1.33) and confidence (b = 0.48, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.88), but not changes to practice (b = 0.52, 95% CI -0.08 to 1.12). The number of sessions attended significantly predicted all three outcomes. As hypothesized, these improvements coincided with a reduction in specialist referrals by intervention group clinicians, per patient assigned to them (b = -0.44, 95% CI -0.62 to -.26), with no significant difference in visit duration or patient load. Our findings provide randomized trial evidence that the ECHO case-based virtual community of practice model can generate improvements to clinician knowledge and confidence in the care of patients with IACC and decreased reliance on specialist referrals. This offers a promising strategy for strengthening primary care capacity to address these complex conditions. Clinicaltrials.gov, identifier NCT05167227.

studies.title: Experiences of individually tailored physical exercise in COVID-19-induced postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: A qualitative content analysis.
studies.authors: Svensson, Annie, Sönnerfors, Pernilla, Holmström, Linda, Nygren-Bonnier, Malin et al.
studies.abstract: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) is a phenotype of post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC), characterised by orthostatic intolerance and a range of debilitating symptoms. Exercise is a frequently implemented intervention in the treatment of POTS and PCC. However, patients' experiences with exercise as a therapeutic modality remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to explore the experiences of individuals diagnosed with PCC and POTS who underwent an individually tailored physical exercise intervention. A qualitative study design with an inductive approach was applied. Twenty-three participants who completed a feasibility study, involving semi-supervised tailored exercise, were recruited for individual interviews. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview guide and analysed through qualitative content analysis. Five main categories emerged, underscoring the importance of individualised design of exercise programs, flexible modalities, and continuous support from physiotherapists with expertise in PCC and POTS. Participants experienced improvements in physical, mental, and social functioning, although setbacks and symptom fluctuation were common. Strategies for energy management, alongside informal and formal support, were identified as facilitators and reduced barriers to exercise as a treatment. Psychological dimensions, including hope, motivation, goal setting, emotional adaptation, acceptance, and coping strategies, were central to participants' experiences. The combination of the intervention structure, therapeutic support, and effective strategies was perceived as contributing to the intervention's effectiveness, and many participants viewed exercise as a key pathway to recovery. This study highlights the need for a flexible and individualised rehabilitation approach in COVID-19-induced POTS. Moreover, exercise should be closely monitored by a physiotherapist with condition-specific expertise, who not only adapts the exercise to symptom fluctuations but also addresses diverse psychosocial needs and individual resources. The participants' experiences indicate that a holistic, multidisciplinary, and person-centred rehabilitation model may support recovery and contribute to improved long-term wellbeing in individuals with PCC and POTS.

studies.title: Bidirectional regulation of pancreatic stellate cell-mediated pancreatic fibrosis by prostaglandin subtypes: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
studies.authors: Wang, Sichun, Chen, Hubo, Wang, Lina
studies.abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a recurrent inflammatory pancreatic disease characterized by progressive parenchymal damage. Currently, there are no effective clinical approaches to halt pancreatic fibrosis progression. As a core mediator involved in inflammation and fibrogenesis, prostaglandin (PG) participates in diverse inflammatory signaling cascades via the arachidonic acid metabolic pathway and further modulates pancreatic stellate cell (PSC) activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. This review systematically summarizes how distinct PG subtypes bind to corresponding receptors to regulate multiple signaling pathways and mediate PSC-related pancreatic fibrosis. It offers novel insights into developing targeted drugs against PG-related pathways and optimizing clinical treatment strategies for pancreatic fibrosis.

studies.title: Herpesvirus reactivation in COVID-19: clinical evidence, mechanistic insights, and research gaps.
studies.authors: Yoo, Jaeyeong, Park, Ji Soo, Kim, Jiyun, Lee, Seung-Hyun et al.
studies.abstract: Herpesviruses establish lifelong latency and can reactivate when antiviral immune surveillance is compromised. Since the onset of COVID-19 pandemic, reactivation of multiple human herpesviruses has increasingly been documented, particularly in patients with severe or critical illness. Herpesvirus reactivation has been associated with prolonged intensive care unit stays, secondary infections, greater ventilatory support requirements, and increased mortality. This review summarizes the latency and reactivation characteristics of the major human herpesviruses and evaluates the clinical evidence linking their reactivation to SARS-CoV-2 infection. We further propose a multifactorial mechanistic framework involving impaired T-cell and natural killer cell surveillance, defective interferon-mediated immunity, sustained inflammation and cytokine signaling, direct and indirect effects of SARS-CoV-2 proteins, and host transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. However, despite accumulating clinical and experimental evidence supporting a biologically plausible association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and herpesvirus reactivation, the precise mechanisms underlying this interplay remain incompletely understood. Longitudinal viral monitoring, physiologically relevant latency models, and mechanistic intervention studies are therefore needed to establish causality and identify patients who may benefit from targeted surveillance or antiviral treatment.

studies.title: Incidence of new-onset pulmonary fibrosis 4.5 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection in an academic urban medical center.
studies.authors: Changela, Sagar, Chintalapati, Bharadwaj, Lightman, Michelle, Duong, Tim Q
studies.abstract: The long-term risk of clinical new-onset pulmonary fibrosis (PF) and its various downstream impacts following SARS-CoV-2 infection remain incompletely characterized in existing literature. A retrospective cohort was analyzed using Montefiore Health System electronic health record data over 4.5 years (March 2020-August 2024). Hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients without prior PF diagnosis were matched 1:2 to COVID-19 negative controls. New-onset PF and subsequent downstream impacts were identified by diagnostic ICD-10 codes. Covariate balance was assessed and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) models were used to estimate PF risk and logistic and Poisson regression models were used to assess post-PF secondary outcomes. Sensitivity analyses included multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional-hazard models, inverse probability weighting and analyses using a pre-pandemic historical control. After propensity score matching, both hospitalized COVID-19 patients (sHR = 2.05; 95% CI [1.69-2.4]) and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients (sHR = 2.33; 95% CI [1.88-2.88]) demonstrated significantly increased risk of PF when compared to COVID-19 negative controls over up to 4.5-year follow-up period. In patients with new-onset PF, prior hospitalization with COVID-19 has associated with higher odds of pneumonia (OR = 4.84 [3.50-6.67]), bronchiolitis (OR = 3.45 [1.12-8.81]), respiratory failure (OR = 3.76 [2.72-5.16]), asthma exacerbation (OR = 2.54 [1.36-4.46]) and COPD exacerbation (OR = 2.91 [1.80-4.58]), whereas non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients exhibited increased odds of pneumonia (OR = 1.98 [1.25-3.06]) and asthma exacerbation (OR = 2.06[1.00-3.86]). Similarly, hospitalized COVID-19 patients showed increased risk of PH (RR = 1.66[1.01-2.71]) and non-hospitalized patients showed an increased risk of PE (RR = 2.68[1.14-6.35]). In a diverse cohort with up to 4.5 years follow-up, we found both hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients have a higher long-term risk of new-onset PF and higher burden of subsequent downstream respiratory complications compared to matched non-COVID-19 controls. These findings demonstrate post-COVID-19 PF as a relevant and clinically significant outcome and suggest the need for long-term surveillance, risk stratification, and targeted intervention.

studies.title: [A brief cognitive-behavioral intervention program for telemedical application in Post-COVID-19 syndrome].
studies.authors: Riese, Dominic, Blume, Kathrin, Merker, Ingrid, Früh, Marlene Sophia et al.
studies.abstract: Due to the high prevalence of psychiatric symptoms among post-COVID patients, there is a clear need for low-threshold psychiatric differential diagnostics and co-treatment. Based on clinical experience with day-clinic and inpatient Post-COVID patients presenting with relevant psychiatric symptoms - such as depressive or anxious affect - Jena University Hospital developed a short-term behavioral therapy intervention for individual settings. This program focuses on psychoeducation, improving coping strategies, and enhancing resource management. The psychotherapeutic manual developed for this purpose is currently being implemented and evaluated via video consultations as part of a three-part treatment program within the WATCH project. Aufgrund der hohen Prävalenz psychiatrischer Symptome bei Post-COVID-Patient:innen ergibt sich die Notwendigkeit einer niedrigschwelligen psychiatrischen Differentialdiagnostik und Mitbehandlung. Aufgrund klinischer Erfahrungen mit teilstationären und stationären Post-COVID-Patient:innen mit relevanter psychiatrischer Symptomatik – wie depressiver oder ängstlicher Affektivität – hat das Universitätsklinikum Jena ein verhaltenstherapeutischen Kurzzeitinterventionsprogramm für das Einzelsetting entwickelt. Dieses zielt auf Psychoedukation, die Verbesserung der Krankheitsverarbeitung und des Ressourcenmanagements ab. Das hierfür entwickelte psychotherapeutische Manual wird aktuell im Rahmen des WATCH-Projekts als Teil eines drei-teiligen Behandlungsprogramms über Videosprechstunden durchgeführt und evaluiert.

studies.title: Changes in self-reported Long COVID in different variant-dominant phases of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: the influence of vaccination on a diverse Israeli cohort study.
studies.authors: Lazar, Sophie, Kuodi, Paul, Shibli, Haneen, Zayyad, Hiba et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) risk varies across SARS-CoV-2 variants, but causal inference is complicated by rising vaccine coverage coinciding with viral evolution. We examined how pre-infection vaccination status modified LC risk across different pandemic periods dominated by different variants, to disentangle the contributions of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity. In this prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021-March 2023, participants completed baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. LC was defined as ≥3 symptoms within validated symptom clusters. Infections were assigned to an infection period corresponding to the predominant circulating variant (Wild type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) at onset time. Pre-infection vaccination was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses). Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Among 1715 participants reporting 2018 infections, LC was reported following 30·4% of infections. In models adjusted for vaccination, LC risk did not differ between the Delta and Omicron-dominant periods (aRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·80-1·26). Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period carried lower LC risk than during Delta (aRR 0·62, 95% CI 0·40-0·98). LC risk did not differ by variant-dominant periods among unvaccinated or fully vaccinated individuals. Observed differences in LC risk at various periods of the pandemic dominated by different variants may be largely explained by concurrent increases in vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the period of variant dominance.

studies.title: Long COVID prevalence among U.S. adults: A state-level ecological analysis of associations with SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization rates, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity.
studies.authors: Zhao, Xinmeng, Deng, Li, Ford, Nicole D, Saydah, Sharon
studies.abstract: Long COVID has emerged as a major public health concern in the United States, yet geographic variation in its prevalence remains poorly understood. This study examines how state-level differences in COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection burden, severity of acute COVID-19 (measured by hospitalization rates) and multimorbidity burden relate to adult Long COVID prevalence in the United States. We conducted an ecological analysis using data from the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), from which we estimated state-level prevalence of self-reported Long COVID among adults. These estimates were linked with publicly available data on SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalizations, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and a multimorbidity indicator (defined as ≥3 chronic conditions associated with increased risk of severe COVID-19, e.g., diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease). Multivariable linear regression models were used to assess the association between these factors and Long COVID prevalence, adjusting for state age and sex distributions. Rubin's rules were applied to propagate the uncertainty in the estimates of Long COVID and COVID-19 vaccine coverage through regression analyses. All examined factors-including SARS-CoV-2 incidence, COVID-19 hospitalization, COVID-19 vaccine coverage, and multimorbidity prevalence-varied by state. In univariable analyses, vaccine coverage and multimorbidity prevalence were significantly associated with Long COVID prevalence. In the multivariable model, vaccine coverage and SARS-CoV-2 incidence were significant; however, after accounting for uncertainty in Long COVID and vaccine coverage estimates, only higher vaccine coverage remained significantly associated with lower Long COVID prevalence. Higher State-level variation in COVID-19 vaccine coverage was consistently associated with lower adult Long COVID prevalence. These ecological findings support further investigation of vaccination and other state-level determinants of Long COVID burden and may inform population-level strategies for addressing Long COVID.

studies.title: Homotypic targeting and fibrosis modulation by human pancreatic stellate cell-derived exosomes.
studies.authors: Zhao, Ruoqi, Shi, Songxuan, Zang, Wenfeng, Wang, Jing et al.
studies.abstract: Extensive desmoplastic remodeling in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) limits the intratumoral access of therapeutic agents and contributes to treatment resistance. Here, we investigated the stromal uptake preference, fibrosis-modulating activity, and siRNA-loading capacity of human pancreatic stellate cell-derived exosomes (HPSC-Exos). HPSC-Exos were recovered through sequential centrifugation steps ending with ultracentrifugation. Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) placed most detected particles within the 100-150 nm range, whereas immunoblotting identified CD9, CD81, and TSG101, but not Calnexin. Flow cytometry and confocal microscopy showed greater HPSC-Exo-associated fluorescence in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) than in PANC-1 and HEK-293T cells. Integrin αv and integrin β1 were detected in HPSC-Exo preparations, and RGD peptide competition reduced CAF uptake, supporting RGD-sensitive, integrin-associated interactions. Unloaded HPSC-Exos reduced fibrosis-associated protein expression and produced concentration-associated decreases in FAP, α-SMA, fibronectin, COL1A1, and COL3A1 mRNA levels by approximately 30-51% at 40 μg/mL. CAF wound closure at 24 h was reduced by approximately 68.6% and 81.7% following treatment with 20 and 40 μg/mL HPSC-Exos, respectively, relative to untreated controls. No significant reduction in the metabolic viability of HPSCs, HEK-293 T cells, or CAFs was observed at concentrations up to 80 μg/mL. Additionally, chemically modified siRNA directed against GLI2 (siGLI2) was incorporated into HPSC-Exos by electroporation, and the loaded preparations retained a predominantly nanoscale size distribution and CAF uptake comparable to unloaded HPSC-Exos. Collectively, HPSC-Exos exhibit preferential CAF-associated uptake and intrinsic modulation of fibrosis-associated phenotypes in vitro, while also supporting siRNA loading, providing a biological platform for further investigation in the PDAC stromal microenvironment.

studies.title: Subacute Thyroiditis Following Third Dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 (mRNA) Vaccine in a Patient with Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma:  A Case Report.
studies.authors: Nagy, Amro, Yaqut, Muhammad, Abbas, Doaa, Mohamed, Amna
studies.abstract: Over 160 cases of subacute thyroiditis (SAT) following COVID-19 vaccination or infection have been reported in the literature. Roughly one-half were attributed to either the first or second dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. We report a rare case of SAT in a 47-year-old male patient with a history of clear cell renal cell carcinoma and advanced chronic kidney disease, among other comorbidities, excluding thyroid disease. After he received the third dose of the Pfizer mRNA vaccine, a deranged thyroid profile was accidentally discovered. His SAT remained asymptomatic and normalized in about six months without treatment. SAT post-COVID vaccination is a self-limiting and rare condition that should be considered in the differential diagnosis of silent thyroiditis.

studies.title: Outcome measures in long COVID clinical trials: a review.
studies.authors: van Rhijn-Brouwer, Femke C C, de Canson, Chloé, VanDerNagel, Joanneke E L, Westerhuis, Xandra et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystem disease that affects approximately 10% of people after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. In the absence of curative treatment, high-quality clinical treatment trials are urgently needed for long COVID. There is significant overlap between long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions, in particular myalgic encephalomyelitis. As such, trial design for long COVID can benefit from prior experience in this field. In this review we explore outcome measures in long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis clinical trials to survey current practices, and provide recommendations for future clinical trials. PubMed and Clinicaltrials.gov were searched for clinical trials on long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis that featured a biomedical intervention. 37 myalgic encephalomyelitis and 68 long COVID trials were identified that used 397 outcome measures in total. We then critically assessed the relevance of these outcome measures for patients. Long COVID trial design could be improved by incorporating outcomes that address important symptom clusters such as post-exertional malaise, dysautonomia and mast cell activation. Clinical assessments, physical tests and biomarkers can supplement patient reported outcome measure data, if safety, feasibility and applicability are carefully considered. Lastly, safety of the intervention is rarely adequately evaluated. We recommend a concerted effort to include patient input at all steps of clinical trial design, execution and evaluation.

studies.title: Long COVID shows IL-1 pathway dysregulation without a discrete circulating biomarker signature.
studies.authors: Muñoz-López, Francisco, Flores-Santamaría, Marissa, Santano, Rebeca, Trigueros, Macedonia et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear. Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed, although it is unknown whether these define distinct biological subtypes or overlapping processes. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 312 individuals, including 139 people with LC (PWLC), 99 COVID-19-recovered controls (both groups sampled a median of 8 months after primary SARS-CoV-2 infection), and 74 uninfected controls, from an unvaccinated population, thereby minimizing major sources of biological and epidemiological variability. Circulating immune and endothelial biomarkers and plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA were assessed, together with serological signatures associated with herpesvirus reactivation and SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral responses. Associations with symptom persistence were analyzed using multivariable models and machine learning approaches. Most soluble biomarker differences primarily distinguished previously infected individuals from uninfected controls rather than PWLC from recovered participants. Increased IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA) levels, together with reduced IL-1β/IL-1RA ratios, were the immune alterations most strongly associated with LC, while P-selectin was the endothelial marker showing a suggestive association with symptom persistence. Plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected at low and comparable frequencies in PWLC and recovered individuals, while Ct values tended to be lower among RNA-positive PWLC not reaching statistical difference. Epstein-Barr virus serological profiles were characterized by lower latency- and higher reactivation-associated responses in PWLC, whereas SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels were comparable between groups. Integrated biomarker profiles discriminated prior infection more effectively than LC status, and expansion to multimodal predictors did not clearly improve discrimination between PWLC and recovered participants. Overall, LC was associated with overlapping immune, endothelial, and virological alterations rather than discrete biomarker-defined subtypes.

studies.title: [Clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors].
studies.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
studies.authors: Druzhkova, O V, Andreeva, I Yu, Severtsev, V V, Khritinin, D F
studies.abstract: To analyze the clinical and pathogenetic heterogeneity of anxiety disorders in COVID-19 survivors to inform differentiated therapeutic approaches. A comparative, observational, prospective study included 90 patients, with the presence of anxiety symptoms after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. The sample was divided into two groups: Group 1 ( Anxiety severity reached moderately severe levels (median scores on HAM-A: 24-25; GAD-7: 16). Asthenia was observed in 87.8% of patients, and cognitive impairment ('brain fog') occurred in 77.8%. Autonomic disorders (A.M. Vein average score 37.4-37.9) included cardiac (53.3%), gastrointestinal (17.8%), and pain syndromes. Three clinically relevant primary psychopathological syndromes were identified: anxiety-asthenic (61.2%), anxiety-hypochondriacal (31.1%), and anxiety-depressive (7.7%). The organic pathway (neuroinflammation) was predominant in the pathogenesis. The somatogenic pathway was associated with autonomic dysfunction and pain syndromes, while the psychogenic (nosogenic) pathway contributed to the development of anxiety-hypochondriacal and anxiety-depressive syndromes. Anxiety disorders in the post-COVID period are highly heterogeneous and require differentiated therapeutic approaches. Pharmacotherapy, including antidepressants and neurometabolic therapy, is indicated for the organic subtype, while psychotherapy should be prioritized for the psychogenic subtype. Анализ клинико-патогенетической гетерогенности тревожных расстройств у пациентов после перенесенного COVID-19 для разработки дифференцированных терапевтических подходов. Проведено сравнительное наблюдательное проспективное исследование. В выборку были включены 90 пациентов с наличием симптомов тревоги после перенесенной инфекции SARS-CoV-2. Выборка была разделена на 2 группы: Группу 1 ( Выраженность тревоги достигала умеренно тяжелых значений (медиана HAM-A: 24—25; ГТР-7: 16). У 87,8% пациентов выявлена астения, у 77,8% — когнитивные нарушения («мозговой туман»). Вегетативные нарушения (средний балл по Вейну 37,4—37,9) включал кардиальные (53,3%), гастроинтестинальные (17,8%) и болевые синдромы. С клинической точки зрения были выделены три основных психопатологических синдрома: тревожно-астенический (61,2%), тревожно-ипохондрический (31,1%) и тревожно-депрессивный (7,7%). С патогенетической точки зрения преобладающим являлся органический путь развития расстройств (нейровоспаление). Соматогенный путь был связан с вегетативной дисфункцией и болевыми синдромами. Психогенный (нозогенный) путь являлся психопатологической основой для формирования тревожно-ипохондрических и тревожно-депрессивных синдромов. Тревожные расстройства в постковидном периоде гетерогенны, что требует дифференцированной терапии: при органическом варианте — фармакотерапии (антидепрессанты, нейрометаболическая терапия), при психогенном — приоритет психотерапии.

studies.title: long covid and subjective wellbeing among U.S. working-age adults.
studies.authors: Wolf, Douglas A, Monnat, Shannon M, Gutin, Iliya, Wiemers, Emily W et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID symptoms can persist for months or years, impeding daily functioning, employment, and social relationships. While prior research links long COVID to adverse clinical mental health outcomes, less attention has been paid to broader subjective wellbeing-including life satisfaction, happiness, and hopefulness. This study examined associations between long COVID symptoms and subjective wellbeing among U.S. working-age adults, including whether associations differ by sex. This cross-sectional analysis used data from the 2023 and 2024 National Wellbeing Surveys (NWS), a weighted survey of U.S. adults aged 18-64 (N = 13,880). We operationalized long COVID as having experienced any of eight symptoms (tiredness or fatigue, difficulty thinking or concentrating or forgetfulness/memory problems, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, joint or muscle pain, fast-beating or pounding heart or chest pain, dizziness on standing, depression, anxiety, or mood changes, and symptoms that get worse after physical or mental activities), a symptom count, and a dose-response specification. Subjective wellbeing measures include life satisfaction, happiness, and hopefulness. We estimated regression models for the full sample and separately by sex, adjusting for sociodemographic and economic characteristics. We reported results using point estimates, odds ratios (ORs) and 95% Confidence Intervals (95% CI). Among all respondents, 39% reported at least one long COVID symptom, with females reporting higher prevalence (43.2%) than males (34.4%) and more symptoms (mean = 1.91) than males (mean = 1.39). In the full sample, long COVID was significantly associated with lower wellbeing across all three subjective wellbeing outcomes for both sexes. A dose-response pattern was observed: having had any symptoms and having more symptoms was associated with worse wellbeing. Among individual symptoms, depression or anxiety and cognitive difficulties exhibited the strongest negative associations with subjective wellbeing. Despite reporting higher long COVID prevalence, females had higher predicted life satisfaction and hopefulness than males at most levels of long COVID severity. In this national sample of U.S. working-age adults, long COVID was associated with reduced subjective wellbeing across multiple operationalizations of long COVID and dimensions of wellbeing for both males and females. These findings underscore that the burden of long COVID extends beyond clinical mental health outcomes to broader evaluative and experiential dimensions of wellbeing, suggesting long COVID may represent an important population health risk for diminished quality of life.

studies.title: Effect of pirfenidone on the short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related acute respiratory distress syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
studies.authors: Long, Meiling, Zhang, Yi, Tong, Jin
studies.abstract: Pirfenidone, approved for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), slows lung function decline and reduces fibrosis, including in post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis. Its early use in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the effects of early pirfenidone administration on short- and long-term outcomes in pulmonary infection-related ARDS. In this prospective cohort study, 97 ARDS patients were consecutively recruited and assigned to Pirfenidone (n = 29), Glucocorticoid (n = 38), or Control (n = 30) groups according to the severity and clinical course of the disease by the attending clinical team, all receiving standard care. Short-term outcomes included 28-day mortality, ICU length of stay, and hospital length of stay. Long-term outcomes at 3 and 6 months included chest CT fibrosis score, pulmonary function [forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)], SpO At 6 months, the Pirfenidone Group had significantly lower chest CT fibrosis scores than the Glucocorticoid Group [3.0 (0.0-6.5) vs. 6.0 (4.0-8.0), p < 0.05], which was comparable to that of the Control Group. FVC, SpO Early pirfenidone administration in pulmonary infection-related ARDS enhances long-term functional recovery and reduces fibrosis without increasing safety risks, although it does not significantly impact short-term outcomes. These findings support the consideration of early antifibrotic therapy in ARDS management.

studies.title: Predicting the persistence of Long COVID 36 months after hospitalisation: a prospective Ukrainian cohort study.
studies.authors: Honchar, Oleksii, Ashcheulova, Tetiana
studies.abstract: To determine early predictive markers and to develop prognostic models for self-reported persistence of Long COVID syndrome at 36 months after hospitalisation. A prospective observational study with cross-sectional analyses at predefined follow-up points. A tertiary care hospital. 221 patients hospitalised for COVID-19 underwent detailed clinical, functional, imaging and survey-based symptom assessment prior to discharge and at 1 month, followed by a 3-year longitudinal follow-up on symptoms. 159 patients (mean age 53.1±13.6 years, 55% female) completed the 36-month assessment and were included in the final analysis. Self-reported persistence of Long COVID symptoms at 36 months after hospital discharge. At 36 months after discharge, 66 (41%) patients reported persistent Long COVID symptoms. This group did not differ in age or sex structure, more frequently reported ongoing symptoms at 3 months (91% vs 59%, p<0.001) and 12 months (77% vs 13%, p<0.001), had longer time to hospitalisation (10.2±3.4 vs 5.2±3.9 days, p<0.001) and higher Charlson comorbidity index (0.61±0.96 vs 0.33±0.56, p=0.022), higher in-hospital creatinine (109 (100–119) vs 96 (85–105) µmol/L, p<0.001), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (43 (37–55) vs 32 (21–47) IU/L, p=0.003), and alanine aminotransferase (47 (30–128) vs 42 (26–62) IU/L, p=0.011) and paradoxically lower Galectin-3 (8.6±0.7 vs 9.0±0.5 ng/mL, p<0.001) and sST2 (23.2±13.7 vs 29.7±15.8 ng/mL, p=0.012). No significant differences were found in inflammatory markers, minimal in-hospital peripheral capillary oxygen saturation, need for oxygen supplementation, pulmonary involvement on CT or lung ultrasound, and clinically negligible differences detected in cardiovascular evaluation, with a baseline tendency to minimal hypercontractility and lower flow-mediated dilation (10.1±5.1 vs 12.9%±5.9%, p=0.006) and marginally worse early dynamics of diastolic indices in Long COVID group. In 6-Minute Walking Test, no differences were observed at baseline but patients with Long COVID reported higher postexertional fatigue (3.3±2.1 vs 1.9±1.6, p<0.001) and dyspnoea (3.4±1.7 vs 2.5±1.8, p=0.027) despite lower blood oxygen desaturation (1.7±1.7 vs 2.8%±2.4%, p=0.014) at 1 month. In symptom assessment, longitudinal trajectories differed significantly for Medical Research Council Dyspnoea (p=0.004), post-COVID functional scale (p<0.001), EFTER-COVID study physical symptoms (p<0.001) and Symptom Burden Questionnaire for Long COVID Memory, Thinking and Communication (p<0.001) scores, reaching maximal differences by 3–12 months, while respiratory scores showed no sustained differences. A simple artificial neural network model combining predischarge variables (sex, age, creatinine, AST, weight loss, duration of hospitalisation and 6-Minute Walk Distance) with 3-month multidimensional symptom assessment achieved a 92% accuracy (area under the receiver operating characteristic, AUROC 0.902), consistently outperforming other machine learning classifiers. A simplified model using only 3-month survey data, age, sex and hospitalisation duration retained high discrimination accuracy (88%, AUROC 0.850). 41% of hospitalised COVID-19 patients reported persistent symptoms at 36 months, preceded by early divergence in patient-reported symptoms despite comparable recovery of objective functional parameters. Predictive models incorporating 3-month multidimensional symptom assessment and routine clinical variables accurately identified patients at risk, outperforming later reassessment strategies and supporting early risk stratification.

studies.title: Making diagnostic recommendations when evidence is lacking: A proposed framework.
studies.authors: Khawandi, Jana, Brignardello-Petersen, Romina, Falcone, Emilia Liana, Santesso, Nancy et al.
studies.abstract: Developing recommendations about test strategies is believed to be challenging, especially when there is no data about the accuracy of the test to diagnose the condition or longitudinal evidence about the effects of the tests on patient important outcomes. We therefore developed a framework to facilitate the discussions of a guideline panel to make diagnostic recommendations. This framework was used when making recommendations for the use of diagnostic tests for post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC) (also known as Long Covid). The framework includes six questions. Four questions address desirable effects: Does a test 1) increase/decrease suspicion of PCC, 2) increase/ decrease suspicion of comorbidities associated with PCC, 3) confirm/ rule out other diagnoses, and 4) change the management. Two questions address undesirable effects: Does a test 1) increase the risk of healthcare overuse, and 2) cause important harm. Answers inform the final judgments about desirable and undesirable effects of a test and are incorporated in the Evidence to Decision Framework to make the recommendation. The proposed framework has been used to make 15 recommendations in one condition and therefore, additional research is needed to assess its application in other conditions and to validate it. Such a framework could play a major role in assisting panels to navigate the tradeoffs between the benefits and harms of tests; enhance transparency in what may have driven the decision; and, help users to better understand how conclusions were reached to make a recommendation. Plain language Summary: When making recommendations for the use of diagnostic tests for post-COVID-19 Condition (PCC), the Canadian Testing, Identification & Diagnosis Related to PCC guideline group members struggled with making judgments on the benefits and harms of the tests. Therefore, a group of guideline methodologists and clinical experts created a framework to help the guideline panel make judgments about whether using a test to diagnose PCC or PCC-related comorbidities would lead to benefits or harms. The framework guided discussions to make recommendations. This framework was used during the development of tests in one guideline only, and it will need further validation. However, the framework could help other guideline panels make recommendations where there is a similar lack of evidence about the effects of the tests.

studies.title: Timing of Long COVID Improvement in Prospectively Followed RECOVER-Adult Participants.
studies.authors: Reeder, Harrison T, Donohue, Sarah E, Martin, Jeffrey N, Hornig, Mady et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. National Institutes of Health.

studies.title: COVID-19 treatments: current options and therapies under investigation.
studies.authors: Opsteen, Skye, Erdmann, Nathaniel
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has contributed to more than 7 million deaths globally and has triggered a variety of postacute sequelae, now commonly referred to as long COVID, in millions more. Early efforts during the pandemic resulted in several therapies to mitigate the severity and mortality of acute COVID-19. However, despite effective therapies and accumulated immunity through vaccination and natural infection reducing disease severity, COVID-19 continues to contribute to hospitalizations and mortality. Long COVID encompasses several distinct yet overlapping clinical syndromes, and evidence suggests that these manifestations are mediated by numerous underlying mechanisms. There are currently no approved therapies for the treatment of long COVID, driven in part by its heterogeneity in presentation and etiology. This review will outline the current guidelines for treating acute COVID-19 and summarize information on the mechanistic rationale behind various published and ongoing clinical trials investigating potential long COVID therapeutic agents.

studies.title: Incidence and Prevalence of Metabolic Syndrome Among Hospital Employees: A Comparison Before and After COVID-19 Pandemic.
studies.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
studies.authors: Luo, Hanqing, Sun, Kai, Wang, Zhenjie, Xu, Tengda
studies.abstract: To investigate metabolic syndrome (MetS) incidence and prevalence in healthcare workers pre- and post-COVID-19 pandemic. The cohort included 3,759 healthcare workers with repeated health examinations from 2014 to 2022. The incidence density and prevalence of MetS (≥3 of 5 components) were compared using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE), adjusted for gender, age and department. MetS prevalence was 20.0% (2014-2016), 26.3% (2017-2019), and 26.2% (2020-2022). The incidence density significantly dropped from 32.8 and 43.4 to 23.8 per 1000 person-years. Unlike the overall decline in most components during the pandemic (2020-2022), hyperglycemia incidence increased steadily throughout the study periods, with the highest pre-pandemic incidence shifting from hypertension to hypertriglyceridemia. The metabolic health of healthcare workers remains a substantial concern, with hypertriglyceridemia and hyperglycemia warranting targeted interventions despite an overall decrease in MetS incidence.

studies.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
studies.authors: Li, Xiang, Chen, Hao, Fu, Wenguang
studies.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

studies.title: Research Landscape of Chronic Pain and Neuropsychiatric Symptoms (1983-2025): A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis.
studies.authors: Quan, Xingpu, Fu, Xinrui, Lu, Tao, Lai, Jiandong et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic pain affects a substantial proportion of the global adult population and is closely associated with neuropsychiatric symptoms, such as depression and anxiety, which may further worsen pain outcomes and increase mortality risk. However, development trends and research hotspots in this field remain insufficiently clarified. This study aimed to provide a macroscopic overview of research on the relationship between chronic pain and neuropsychiatric symptoms and to identify future directions for research and clinical practice, with particular attention to interdisciplinary collaboration and personalized treatment strategies. A total of 3627 publications between 1983 and 2025 were included in the final analysis. Bibliometric analyses and visualizations were performed using the R-based Bibliometrix package, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Microsoft Excel 2019. The number of publications in this field showed a steady upward trend, with rapid growth after 2017. Among contributing countries, the United States emerged as the most active contributor and demonstrated the strongest international collaboration. Leading institutions, including Harvard University; high-impact journals, such as Neurology and Headache; and influential researchers, such as Lipton RB, made prominent contributions to the field. Keyword co-occurrence, citation burst, and thematic evolution analyses indicated that "chronic pain," "pain management," "migraine," "depression," and "anxiety" remained central research themes, whereas "long COVID," "mental health," and "quality of life" may represent emerging future research directions. Research in this field is increasingly shifting toward integrated pain management that incorporates neuropsychiatric and psychosocial dimensions. Future academic and clinical efforts should prioritize the development of individualized treatment frameworks to optimize patient outcomes and refine existing pain management protocols.

studies.title: Measuring infectious disease stigma in the German population: Psychometric properties of stigma scales related to COVID-19, Long Covid and non-vaccination in a representative population sample.
studies.journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
studies.authors: Menzinger, Jule, Alpers, Carlotta, McLaren, Thomas, Danqa, Dafina et al.
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was widely accompanied by stigma towards certain groups of people, which can diminish efforts of disease control and exacerbate negative impacts of the disease itself. Research on COVID-19-related stigma in the German population is scarce and, internationally, is lacking validated and standardized measurement instruments. To address this issue, this study tested the psychometric properties of a set of scales to measure COVID-19-related stigma in a representative sample of the German population. Overall, 1960 people (M(SD)age = 49.8(17.3) years, 55.8% female) participated in a nationally representative cross-sectional survey in Germany. Six scales were tested, assessing public attitudes towards people who have had COVID-19 (COVID-PSS), those who had the disease multiple times (MI-PSS), people with Long Covid (LC-PSS) and people who chose not to get vaccinated (nonVac-PSS). We further assessed internalized stigma of individuals, who have had COVID-19 at least once (COINS) and those who chose not to get vaccinated (nonVac-IS). All scales were tested for their intended factorial structure through confirmatory factor analysis, convergent and discriminant validity and reliability. All scales, excepting the scale for internalized stigma of unvaccinated individuals, showed good to excellent fit indices and factor loadings, supporting their intended factorial structure. Convergent and discriminant validity were established for the public stigma scales. The COINS did not converge with a measure of quality of life, but with depressive symptoms, whereas the nonVac-IS did not show convergence with presumed related constructs. Reliability coefficients showed good internal consistency among the items. Five out of the six scales proved to be valid tools to measure stigmatizing attitudes related to COVID-19, Long Covid and non-vaccination in a German sample. The scales hold promises for monitoring stigma during infectious disease outbreaks and informing the development of public health interventions to counteract health-related stigma.

studies.title: Biopsychosocial versus purely biological explanation for persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19: An experimental study with lay participants and healthcare professionals.
studies.authors: Lebrun, Héloïse, Petzke, Tara, Stone, Jon, Ranque, Brigitte et al.
studies.abstract: This study aims to compare changes of attitudes regarding the causation, evolution, and treatment for persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19 after lay participants and healthcare professionals receive medical explanations presenting either a purely biological or a biopsychosocial account of symptoms. Participants completed an online questionnaire assessing their views on underlying physical and mental causation, chronicity, disability and annoyance of symptoms, required examinations, and appropriate treatments. Lay participants rated their feelings of offence and anxiety associated with symptoms, while healthcare professionals their feelings of competence and willingness to care for a patient with persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19. All participants were allocated alternatingly to watch a standardized video with distinct accounts: either purely biological or biopsychosocial. -tests were used to compare representations after explanations. A total of 208 lay participants (mean age: 42; 74% women) and 104 healthcare professionals (mean age: 42; 68% women) were included. The two explanations were efficient in changing beliefs about mental and physical causation of persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19 in both participants' groups. Compared to the purely biological explanation, the biopsychosocial explanation increased feelings of offence while at the same time decreasing lay participants' views that symptoms are chronic and disabling and increasing views that symptoms can be improved with CBT and physical exercise therapy. In healthcare professionals, the biopsychosocial explanation increased feelings of competence and belief that symptoms can be improved with CBT. A standardized biopsychosocial video explanation may help promoting integrative care. Results suggest that explaining the biopsychosocial approach can modulate healthcare professionals' and lay people's attitudes towards persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19. Future research should investigate how explaining the biopsychosocial approach can be further improved to promote more sustained changes in attitudes over time.

studies.title: Ultrasound-Triggered HSC Membrane-Cloaked Nanotherapeutics Attenuate Liver Fibrosis via Simultaneous Modulation of Mitophagic Flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 Cascade.
studies.authors: Li, Han-Mei, Ye, Li-Tao, Leng, Yi-Han, Wang, Ping-Zi et al.
studies.abstract: This study presents an ultrasound-triggered therapeutic platform based on melatonin-loaded and perfluoropentane-encapsulated mesoporous silica nanoparticles, which are further cloaked with activated hepatic stellate cell membranes (HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs), designed for the precision treatment of liver fibrosis. This innovative drug delivery system leverages the inherent targeting properties of cell membrane coatings, effectively functioning as a "gatekeeper" that prevents premature drug release. By incorporating melatonin and perfluoropentane (PFP), our approach enables ultrasound-mediated controlled release, enhancing therapeutic efficacy. In vitro investigations revealed that upon ultrasound activation, HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs significantly inhibited the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and alleviated mitochondrial damage. Mechanistic studies employing Western blot analysis revealed that this nanotherapeutic strategy was associated with altered expression of autophagy-related proteins, including a reduced LC3-II/I ratio, increased P62 accumulation, and downregulated PINK1/Parkin. These findings suggest an overall suppression of autophagic activity, encompassing both general autophagy and mitophagy; however, a causal link remains to be established. Furthermore, using a rat model of liver fibrosis, robust histological assessments (including HE, Masson, Sirius Red, and α-SMA staining) demonstrated that our system markedly ameliorated fibrotic lesions under precise ultrasound guidance. This research introduces a novel strategy that integrates targeted delivery, controlled drug release, and visualizable therapeutic outcomes, thereby representing a significant advancement in the management of liver diseases. By simultaneously modulating mitophagic flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 signaling cascade, our HM-Mel@PFP-MSN-based nanotherapeutics open new avenues for liver fibrosis treatment, emphasizing the potential of leveraging ultrasound in enhancing therapeutic precision and efficacy.
